public.text: I would challenge a prior assumption that anything should be protected from re-invention including existing standards
public.suggestedRevision:
While referring to existing established, dominant even good standards, it works against the general intentions of DPI to explicitly name anything but a proven ideal standard. The later description does mitigate somewhat but I would recommend mimising the implication that something is "approved"
The final paragraph describes adaptors but I would suggest making this explicit as an operational delivery compromise rather than the answer to the boundary/replacement challenges for an true interoperability
All this is particularly important where alternatives to structure are entertained as in comment #19
